title: A Lean redesign of tuberculosis contact evaluation in a city public health program
abstract: Problem: 71 percent of contacts completed evaluation within 60 days against a 90 percent target. Intervention: value stream mapping and redesign (home blood draw, direct result routing, same-visit X-ray booking, interpreters at every step). Measures: 60-day completion by index-case month cohort, time to completion, cascade losses, nurse hours and completion for hardest-to-reach contacts. Results will be written after December 2027.
introduction: Contact evaluation for tuberculosis loses people at every handoff, most often between a positive test and the radiograph. Lean redesign and home testing improved completion in other programs.
methods: Two mapping days produced a future-state map, and changes were introduced one at a time. Completion was charted by index-case month cohort from a checked monthly extract, with rules fixed before the first change.
results: No data have been collected yet. The report will show cohort charts with changes marked, cascade losses by step, nurse hours per case and quarterly completion for the hardest-to-reach contacts.
discussion: The discussion will relate chart signals to the changes and report equity groups separately. It will state which changes the program keeps.
limitations: This is a single program with a before-and-after design. Radiology booking lies outside program control.
conclusion: To be written after the last cohort closes. It will report whether the 85 percent aim was met without widening gaps.
